To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated that human CD34+ hematopoeitic progenitor cells transduced with c-mpl, can rescue multi-lineage hematopoeisis in SCID-hu Thy/ Liv implants during HIV-1 in vitro infection and that the differentiated progeny cells carry the HLA class I phenotypes of the donor cells in the recipient animals.

we have introduced the c-Mpl proto-oncogene into CD34+ hematopoeitic stem cells via lentiviral transduction and reconstituted these transduced cells into human fetal thymi/livers in SCID-hu Thy/liv animals.
the lentiviral c-mpl construct can be used for gene therapy of cytopenias in patients with HIV-1 infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of gene therapy to address the hematologic complications in HIV infected patients, which are a common cause of morbidity and mortality.
the development of a gene therapeutic approach to address the cytopenia and immunodeficiency arising in AIDS patients.
the development of gene therapeutic strategies to address the morbimortality resulting from cytopenia, a common and serious complication of HIV/AIDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully demonstrated that the c-mpl proto-oncogene is capable of rescuing multilineage hematopoiesesis in HIV-1 infected CD34+ cells in vitro and in vivo, in SCID-hu mice.
c-mpl is an important genetic element in the gene therapy of HIV infected patients.
we have successfully demonstrated that the lentivirus pRLsinPPT-CMPL can transduce the CD34+ cells and rescue multi-lineage hematopoeisis in the SCID-hu Thy/liver model of HIV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the c-mpl receptor gene is a useful therapeutic target for the treatment of cytopenias in AIDS patients.

the c-mpl expression in CD34+ cells can rescue multi-lineage hematopoesis, in HIV-1 infected SCID-hu Thy/liv implants, and that the progeny of these transduced CD34 cells carry the donor HLA Class I phenotypes.
we show that lentiviral transduction of CD34+ cells with the c-m-pl gene can rescue the multi-lineage differentiation of these hematopoietic cells during in vivo HIV-1 infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the c-mpl expressing progeny of the reconstituted CD 34+ cells, are capable of rescuing myelopoieses, erythropoietes, megakaryopoietes, and lymphoid cells in the thymus, and the rescue is not affected by the effects of the HIV-1 infection on the reconstituting CD34+ cells in vivo.

we show the feasibility of using lentiviruses to deliver the c-mpl proto-oncogene to CD34+ hematopietic progenitor cell populations and the ability of the transduced cells to rescue multi-lineage hematopoeisis during HIV-1 infections in vivo.
c-mpl gene therapy can be used in HIV infected patients to rescue multi-lineage hematopoesis, and thus prevent the cytopenias and the resulting complications in HIV/AIDS patients.
